Subject: Re: Fwd: Production spike: 429s and timeouts across API (started 07:58 UTC)

Looking at logs and routing traces. Quick notes:
- I see a tiering-sync job completed at 07:45 UTC that reassigned ~32 projects to a lower org-tier (probable cause).
- That change reduced effective rate limits for several BrightWell projects. Client retries then flooded the lower tier and produced 429s.

Immediate plan I can run now (15–20m):
1) pause the tiering-sync job (if still running).
2) revert the tier assignment for BrightWell projects to previous mapping (DB rollback + reload).
3) bump project-level quotas temporarily for 2 hours to drain backlog.

If Jonas is available to run the DB rollback + config reload, I can coordinate. Vivek — can you confirm whether the rollback path is safe for today?

-Marissa
Director, Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rachel.kim@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-05T09:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production spike: 429s and timeouts across API (started 07:58 UTC)

Confirming Marissa's observation. Quick diagnostics summary:
- Tiering-sync at 07:45 UTC introduced a mapping regression: alias -> tier lookup fell back to default-low for orgs with an unrecognized alias. BrightWell projects matched that fallback.
- Rate limiter enforced new lower tokens/sec and burst windows. Client-side exponential retries then created a retry storm.

Recommended immediate actions (executing now):
- Start rollback of tiering mapping (run rollback-script v1.3) — runtime ~8m.
- Temporarily increase project quotas for the affected project IDs by +3x for 1 hour (manual override).
- Add a short-lived global retry-shedding rule for calls from BrightWell org (suppress retries for 60s) — reduces amplification.

I've attached the diagnostic bundle and the runbook. Jonas: please approve/execute the override & rollback; I will watch the deploy and metrics.

-Vivek
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: throttle-logs.tar.gz (120MB), support-runbook.md (8KB)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-10-05T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production spike: 429s and timeouts across API (started 07:58 UTC)

Rolling back now — started DB revert at 11:02 UTC (rollback-script v1.3).
Progress updates:
- 11:08 UTC: config reload completed on tiering service for production region us-east-1.
- 11:12 UTC: applied manual project quota overrides for the three affected BrightWell project IDs.
- 11:20 UTC: metrics show 429 rate declining from 22% -> 4% over 8 minutes.

Please hold off on any other automated cutovers for next 2 hours. Naomi/Monica: recommend a short status note to BrightWell (we can be specific about rollback + temporary quota bump; avoid implementation details).

-Jonas
Ops Lead, Live Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Hi Naomi/Monica — quick executive summary for BrightWell and for internal leadership:
- Incident: sudden surge of 429s and timeouts affecting BrightWell production flows starting ~07:58 UTC on 2026-10-05.
- Root cause: tiering-sync mapping regression (alias->tier fallback to default-low) that reduced effective rate limits for BrightWell projects.
- Mitigation executed: tiering mapping rollback (rollback-script v1.3) and temporary +3x project quota overrides. Temporary retry-shedding rule applied while queues drained.
- Impact: peak error rate ~22%. After rollback and quotas, 429s dropped to baseline ~0.6% by 11:30 UTC. No data loss.
- Next steps (owners):
  - Marissa: patch sync job to add strict alias validation and prevent fallback to default-low (ETA 2026-10-07).
  - Vivek/Jonas: add an automated canary for tiering changes and a one-click rollback in the console (ETA 2026-10-14).
  - Naomi: send customer-facing post-incident note with timeline and mitigations (I can draft).

Attachments: diagnostic bundle, logs (attached earlier).

Rachel Kim
Account Lead — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
